question: According to the Colorado CDL Manual, how far can the danger zone extend from the front bumper of a school bus?
choice_a: 50 feet
choice_b: 20 feet
choice_c: 30 feet
choice_d: 10 feet
explanation: The danger zone may extend as much as 30 feet from the front bumper of the school bus, with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-107

question: Why does the Colorado CDL Manual say the area to the left of a school bus is always considered dangerous?
choice_a: Because the stop-signal arm is mounted on that side
choice_b: Because of passing cars
choice_c: Because the driver's blind spot is largest there
choice_d: Because students always exit on that side
explanation: The manual states the area to the left of the bus is always considered dangerous because of passing cars.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-107

question: When properly adjusted, the outside left and right side flat mirrors on a Colorado school bus should allow the driver to see how far behind the bus?
choice_a: 400 feet or 8 bus lengths
choice_b: 200 feet or 4 bus lengths
choice_c: 100 feet or 2 bus lengths
choice_d: 50 feet or 1 bus length
explanation: Flat mirrors should be adjusted so the driver can see 200 feet or 4 bus lengths behind the bus, along the sides of the bus, and the rear tires touching the ground.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-108

question: What is the primary purpose of the outside left and right side crossover mirrors on a Colorado school bus?
choice_a: To see traffic in the adjacent lane while driving on the highway
choice_b: To see the front bumper danger zone directly in front of the bus that is not visible by direct vision
choice_c: To check tire tread depth during a pre-trip inspection
choice_d: To monitor passenger activity inside the bus
explanation: Crossover mirrors are mounted at the front corners of the bus and are used to see the front bumper 'danger zone' area not visible by direct vision, as well as the side danger zones near the service door and front wheel area.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-108 to 10-109

question: According to the manual, when are more students killed in relation to a school bus?
choice_a: While riding as passengers inside the bus
choice_b: While waiting at home for the bus to arrive
choice_c: While walking to a bus stop more than a mile away
choice_d: While getting on or off the bus
explanation: The manual states that more students are killed while getting on or off a school bus each year than are killed as passengers inside of a school bus, making loading and unloading procedures critical.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-109

question: If equipped, when should a Colorado school bus driver activate alternating flashing amber warning lights when approaching a stop?
choice_a: Only when it is dark outside
choice_b: At least 200 feet or approximately 5-10 seconds before the stop, or in accordance with state law
choice_c: Only after the bus has come to a complete stop
choice_d: At least 500 feet before the stop
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to activate alternating flashing amber warning lights at least 200 feet or approximately 5-10 seconds before the school bus stop, or in accordance with state law.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-109 to 10-110

question: When stopping to load or unload students at a designated stop, how far away from the students should the front bumper of the school bus be positioned?
choice_a: At least 10 feet
choice_b: At least 30 feet
choice_c: At least 20 feet
choice_d: At least 5 feet
explanation: The bus should come to a full stop with the front bumper at least 10 feet away from students at the designated stop, forcing students to walk to the bus so the driver has a better view of their movements.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-110

question: After exiting the bus at a route stop, how far should students walk from the side of the bus before the driver may pull away?
choice_a: At least 25 feet
choice_b: At least 15 feet
choice_c: At least 5 feet
choice_d: At least 10 feet
explanation: Students should be told to exit the bus and walk at least 10 feet away from the side of the bus to a position where the driver can plainly see all students before the bus moves.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-110 to 10-111

topic: Crossing in Front of the Bus
question: When a student must cross the roadway after exiting the bus, where should the student stop and wait so the driver can see the student's feet?
choice_a: At the left edge of the roadway
choice_b: Back at the bus door
choice_c: At the right edge of the roadway
choice_d: Directly in front of the bumper
explanation: Students should walk to a location at least 10 feet in front of the right corner of the bumper and stop at the right edge of the roadway, where the driver should be able to see the student's feet.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-111

question: What should a student do if they drop an object near the school bus during loading or unloading?
choice_a: Immediately go back and pick it up before boarding
choice_b: Leave the object, move to a point of safety outside the danger zones, and try to get the driver's attention
choice_c: Ask another student to retrieve it while the bus waits
choice_d: Wait beside the object until the bus door opens again
explanation: Students should be told to leave any dropped object and move to a point of safety out of the danger zones, then attempt to get the driver's attention to retrieve it, since stopping to pick it up could cause the student to disappear from the driver's sight at a dangerous moment.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-112

question: Under which of the following conditions does the Colorado CDL Manual say the driver MUST evacuate the school bus?
choice_a: The heater is not working properly
choice_b: The bus is running more than 15 minutes behind schedule
choice_c: The bus is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing
choice_d: A student requests to be let off early
explanation: Mandatory evacuation conditions listed in the manual include the bus being on fire or threatened by fire, stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing, imminent danger of collision, the bus's position changing to increase danger, or a hazardous materials spill.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-112 to 10-113

question: As a general rule, how far off the road, in the direction of oncoming traffic, should a designated safe place be located during a school bus evacuation?
choice_a: At least 200 feet
choice_b: At least 150 feet
choice_c: At least 50 feet
choice_d: At least 100 feet
explanation: A safe place should be at least 100 feet off the road in the direction of oncoming traffic, to keep students from being hit by debris if another vehicle collides with the bus.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-113

question: If there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials during a bus evacuation, how far upwind of the bus should students be led?
choice_a: At least 100 feet
choice_b: At least 500 feet
choice_c: At least 300 feet
choice_d: At least 200 feet
explanation: The manual instructs that students should be led upwind of the bus at least 300 feet if there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-113

question: According to the manual, when should a driver avoid moving a student believed to have suffered a neck or spinal injury during an evacuation?
choice_a: Unless another adult is present to help
choice_b: Unless the student requests to be moved
choice_c: Unless the student's life is in immediate danger
choice_d: Always, under all circumstances
explanation: The manual states not to move a student believed to have suffered a neck or spinal injury unless his or her life is in immediate danger, and that special procedures must be used to move such victims to prevent further injury.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-113

question: What is a 'passive' railroad-highway crossing, as described in the Colorado CDL Manual?
choice_a: A crossing with only a stop sign for cross traffic
choice_b: A crossing with no traffic control device, where the driver must decide if it is safe to cross
choice_c: A crossing controlled by a police officer
choice_d: A crossing with flashing red lights and gates
explanation: A passive crossing has no type of traffic control device; the decision to proceed rests entirely with the driver, who must recognize the crossing, search for a train, and decide if there is sufficient clear space to cross safely.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-113

question: At a railroad-highway crossing with gates, what should a school bus driver do after the lights begin flashing and until the train has passed?
choice_a: Honk the horn continuously until the gate rises
choice_b: Back away from the crossing immediately
choice_c: Proceed carefully around the gate if no train is visible
choice_d: Remain stopped until the gates go up and the lights have stopped flashing
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to stop when the lights begin to flash and before the gate lowers, then remain stopped until the gates go up and the lights have stopped flashing; if the gate stays down after the train passes, the driver should call the dispatcher rather than drive around it.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-114

question: When stopping at a railroad-highway crossing, how close to the nearest rail should the front of the school bus stop?
choice_a: Not less than 25 feet, not more than 75 feet
choice_b: Exactly 20 feet from the nearest rail
choice_c: Not less than 5 feet, not more than 15 feet
choice_d: Not less than 15 feet, not more than 50 feet
explanation: The manual directs the driver to stop the front of the bus within 50 feet, but not less than 15 feet, from the nearest rail.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-115

question: In Colorado, school buses are NOT required to stop at railroad crossings under which of the following conditions?
choice_a: Crossings controlled by an 'Exempt Crossing' sign
choice_b: Any crossing with fewer than two tracks
choice_c: Crossings located within city limits
choice_d: Crossings located on state highways
explanation: The manual states that in Colorado, school buses are not required to stop at crossings controlled by an 'Exempt Crossing' sign, at crossings controlled by a green traffic signal, or where the crossing is controlled by a police officer or human flag person.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-115

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, how far from the crossing should a school bus driver activate the 4-way hazard lamps to alert other motorists?
choice_a: Not less than 300 feet
choice_b: Not less than 500 feet
choice_c: Not less than 200 feet
choice_d: Not less than 100 feet
explanation: The manual states that the 4-way hazard lamps are activated not less than 200 feet from the railroad crossing to alert other motorists of the pending stop.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-114 to 10-115

question: Under the Department of Transportation requirement cited in the manual, air brake vehicles such as buses must be equipped with antilock braking systems (ABS) if built on or after what date?
choice_a: March 1, 1996
choice_b: March 1, 1998
choice_c: March 1, 1999
choice_d: January 1, 2000
explanation: The Department of Transportation requires ABS on air brake vehicles, including trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies, built on or after March 1, 1998.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-116

question: In emergency braking on a Colorado school bus equipped with ABS, what should the driver avoid doing?
choice_a: Using only the braking force necessary to stop safely
choice_b: Braking the same way as always
choice_c: Steering around an obstacle while braking
choice_d: Pumping the brakes
explanation: The manual states that drivers should brake the same way regardless of whether the bus has ABS, but in emergency braking they should not pump the brakes on a bus equipped with ABS.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-116

question: What does the Colorado CDL Manual say about backing a school bus?
choice_a: It should be used whenever possible to save time
choice_b: It is strongly discouraged and should be done only when there is no other safe way to move the vehicle
choice_c: It is only permitted with two lookouts posted
choice_d: It requires no special precautions if mirrors are properly adjusted
explanation: Backing a school bus is strongly discouraged; the driver should back the bus only when there is no other safe way to move the vehicle, and should never back it when students are outside the bus.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-116 to 10-117

question: According to the manual, how much tail swing can a school bus have, which the driver must monitor with mirrors during turns?
choice_a: Up to 2 feet
choice_b: Up to 3 feet
choice_c: Up to 1 foot
choice_d: Up to 5 feet
explanation: A school bus can have up to a three-foot tail swing, so the driver needs to check mirrors before and during any turning movements to monitor it.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-117

question: According to the manual, when may a school bus driver cross light rail vehicle (LRV) tracks in the Denver metropolitan area?
choice_a: Only when the entire vehicle's length can safely clear the tracks
choice_b: At any time if the hazard lights are activated
choice_c: As soon as one LRV has passed, regardless of others
choice_d: Only when a crossing guard signals, even without checking for trains
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to never cross the light rail tracks until the entire vehicle's length can safely clear the tracks, and to never back across light rail tracks.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 10 - School Bus, p. 10-117 to 10-118
